intake.md.name: intake.md
intake.md.content:
# Lumina coworking

## Original brief

Design a database for Lumina, a coworking platform with 3 locations. Members subscribe to monthly plans and book meeting rooms or desks. Members can optionally select a preferred space. Spaces have shared amenities, capacities, and hourly rates. Track membership history, bookings (confirmed, completed, cancelled), and invoices. Support 5,000 members, 100,000 bookings per year, staff reporting and concurrent booking requests. Retain billing history and protect member contact details.

## Initial understanding

A multi-location coworking platform manages member profiles, plan subscriptions, bookable spaces, shared amenities, reservations, and billing history. Staff need occupancy and revenue reporting; members need safe concurrent booking and privacy boundaries.

## Actors

- Members booking workspaces
- Location staff managing spaces and bookings
- Billing administrators reviewing invoices

## Candidate entities

- Members: name, email, signup date
- Plans: monthly price and included hours
- Memberships: plan and effective dates
- Spaces: location, capacity, hourly rate
- Amenities and space-amenity links
- Bookings: member, space, time range, status
- Invoices: member, issue date, amount, payment state

## Main processes

- Register a member and enroll in a plan
- Search availability and reserve a workspace
- Cancel or complete a booking
- Issue invoices and report occupancy/revenue

## Questions and risks

- Overlapping reservations require transactional enforcement, not a row-level CHECK
- Billing retention and deletion policy need confirmation
- Clarify timezone and cancellation semantics

requirements.md.content:
# Requirements — Lumina coworking

**Status:** Interview complete

## System brief

Design a database for Lumina, a coworking platform with 3 locations. Members subscribe to monthly plans and book meeting rooms or desks. Members can optionally select a preferred space. Spaces have shared amenities, capacities, and hourly rates. Track membership history, bookings (confirmed, completed, cancelled), and invoices. Support 5,000 members, 100,000 bookings per year, staff reporting and concurrent booking requests. Retain billing history and protect member contact details.

## Consolidated requirements

Members need full name, unique email, joined date, active flag, and an optional preferred space. Plans have unique names, monthly price, and included hours. Spaces have a location, unique name per location, capacity and hourly rate. Bookings use UTC start/end and confirmed/completed/cancelled states. Invoices track issue/due dates, amount and draft/paid/overdue states.

Members have many historical memberships; a membership has one member and one plan. A member can optionally choose one preferred space; a space can be preferred by many members. Members make many bookings, each for one space. Spaces share amenities through a many-to-many link. Each invoice belongs to one member; invoices can exist without bookings.

5,000 initial members, 100,000 bookings/year, 3 locations growing to 10, around 30% annual data growth. Keep invoices for seven years and bookings for two years.

Frequent availability searches by location and time, daily staff booking lists, member booking history, monthly occupancy, and overdue-invoice reports. Roughly 20 reads per write.

No overlapping confirmed bookings for a space. The application serializes reservations with a per-space lock and an overlap query inside the same transaction. Invoice status transitions are atomic and idempotent. Around 50 concurrent reservations at peak.

Members only access their own records. Staff can manage bookings for assigned locations; only billing admins see invoices. No payment card details or passwords stored here. Anonymize contact data instead of deleting retained billing evidence.

Booking end must follow start; dates use UTC. Capacity must be positive, rates and invoice amounts nonnegative, emails unique, and due date cannot precede issue date. Cancelled bookings remain for audit and do not block availability.

Yes, lock the space row during each booking transaction and reject any intersecting confirmed interval. Back-to-back reservations are allowed. Members can have multiple non-overlapping memberships over time; enforcing membership interval exclusivity is also a transaction-level policy.

Retain invoice records for seven years, keep a minimal anonymized member record as their FK target, and store all booking timestamps as UTC. Cancellation retains the original reservation and its status.

## Interview round 1

### Entities & attributes

**Question:** Which attributes do members, spaces, plans, bookings, and invoices need?

**Answer:** Members need full name, unique email, joined date, active flag, and an optional preferred space. Plans have unique names, monthly price, and included hours. Spaces have a location, unique name per location, capacity and hourly rate. Bookings use UTC start/end and confirmed/completed/cancelled states. Invoices track issue/due dates, amount and draft/paid/overdue states.

### Relationships & cardinality

**Question:** Can members hold multiple memberships, and can spaces share the same amenities?

**Answer:** Members have many historical memberships; a membership has one member and one plan. A member can optionally choose one preferred space; a space can be preferred by many members. Members make many bookings, each for one space. Spaces share amenities through a many-to-many link. Each invoice belongs to one member; invoices can exist without bookings.

### Volume & growth

**Question:** How much data and annual growth should the platform support?

**Answer:** 5,000 initial members, 100,000 bookings/year, 3 locations growing to 10, around 30% annual data growth. Keep invoices for seven years and bookings for two years.

### Queries & reporting

**Question:** Which availability searches, reports, and write operations matter most?

**Answer:** Frequent availability searches by location and time, daily staff booking lists, member booking history, monthly occupancy, and overdue-invoice reports. Roughly 20 reads per write.

### Transactions & concurrency

**Question:** How should simultaneous reservations and payment updates behave?

**Answer:** No overlapping confirmed bookings for a space. The application serializes reservations with a per-space lock and an overlap query inside the same transaction. Invoice status transitions are atomic and idempotent. Around 50 concurrent reservations at peak.

### Security & privacy

**Question:** Who can access member contact details, bookings, and billing data?

**Answer:** Members only access their own records. Staff can manage bookings for assigned locations; only billing admins see invoices. No payment card details or passwords stored here. Anonymize contact data instead of deleting retained billing evidence.

### Business rules

**Question:** What cancellation, pricing, invoice, and date-range rules must always hold?

**Answer:** Booking end must follow start; dates use UTC. Capacity must be positive, rates and invoice amounts nonnegative, emails unique, and due date cannot precede issue date. Cancelled bookings remain for audit and do not block availability.



## Interview round 2

### Transactions & concurrency

**Question:** You require no double bookings: should reservations lock the space in a transaction, and may bookings be back-to-back?

**Answer:** Yes, lock the space row during each booking transaction and reject any intersecting confirmed interval. Back-to-back reservations are allowed. Members can have multiple non-overlapping memberships over time; enforcing membership interval exclusivity is also a transaction-level policy.

### Security & privacy

**Question:** You need privacy and seven-year billing retention: should contact details be anonymized while invoices keep their member link?

**Answer:** Retain invoice records for seven years, keep a minimal anonymized member record as their FK target, and store all booking timestamps as UTC. Cancellation retains the original reservation and its status.



## Interview decision

All seven dimensions are covered. Follow-up confirmed half-open booking intervals, per-space transaction locks, membership exclusivity, UTC, and privacy-preserving invoice retention.

## Outstanding questions

- None identified.

dbms-choice.md.content:
# DBMS selection

## Selected: PostgreSQL

PostgreSQL fits the multi-user transactional workload, 100,000 bookings per year, 50 concurrent reservations, reporting joins, and seven-year invoice history. Strong constraints and row locks support the documented per-space booking transaction. SQLite remains excellent for an embedded prototype, but is not the preferred concurrent production target.

## Requirements-based comparison

Scores are relative suitability judgments for this workload, not measured performance benchmarks.

| DBMS | Fit / 10 | Strengths | Trade-offs | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PostgreSQL | 9 | Rich constraints, row locks, analytical joins, transactional integrity | Requires a managed or self-hosted database and operational care | Selected for concurrency and reporting requirements |
| MySQL | 8 | Mature InnoDB transactions, accessible managed hosting | Need careful locking and a version with enforced CHECK constraints | Viable alternative; PostgreSQL better matches rich integrity needs |
| SQLite | 5 | Zero-service deployment and excellent local prototyping | Single-writer limits and no server-side row locking for multi-instance writes | Rejected for the anticipated concurrent production workload |
| SQL Server | 7 | Strong enterprise reporting, transactions and access controls | More operational/licensing considerations; no Microsoft-stack requirement | Rejected absent an existing Microsoft ecosystem requirement |

## Source of decision

Based on the original brief and all 2 completed interview rounds in requirements.md.

conceptual-model.md.content:
# Conceptual model — Lumina coworking platform

**Design version:** 2 · **Target:** PostgreSQL

A normalized relational model separates members, product plans, subscription history, spaces, shared amenities, reservations, and invoices. An associative table represents shared amenities. Financial and reservation history remain linked to anonymizable member records.

## Entities

### members

Member identity, optional preferred space and contact information, separable from retained financial history.

### plans

Subscription products with stable pricing and included workspace hours.

### memberships

Effective-dated member subscriptions preserving plan enrollment history.

### spaces

Bookable rooms and desks, each with a location label, capacity and hourly rate.

### amenities

Reusable amenity definitions shared by multiple bookable spaces.

### space_amenities

Associative relation implementing the many-to-many space-to-amenity relationship.

### bookings

UTC reservation intervals with lifecycle state and an optional member-supplied note.

### invoices

Retained member invoices independent of optional booking activity; no payment card data.

## Entity-relationship diagram

```mermaid
erDiagram
  members {
    integer id PK
    string full_name
    string email
    date joined_on
    boolean active
    integer preferred_space_id FK
    string phone
  }
  spaces |o--o{ members : "preferred_space_id"
  plans {
    integer id PK
    string name
    decimal monthly_price
    integer included_hours
  }
  memberships {
    integer id PK
    integer member_id FK
    integer plan_id FK
    date starts_on
    date ends_on
  }
  members ||--o{ memberships : "member_id"
  plans ||--o{ memberships : "plan_id"
  spaces {
    integer id PK
    string name
    string location
    integer capacity
    decimal hourly_rate
  }
  amenities {
    integer id PK
    string name
  }
  space_amenities {
    integer space_id PK,FK
    integer amenity_id PK,FK
  }
  spaces ||--o{ space_amenities : "space_id"
  amenities ||--o{ space_amenities : "amenity_id"
  bookings {
    integer id PK
    integer member_id FK
    integer space_id FK
    timestamp starts_at
    timestamp ends_at
    string status
    text note
  }
  members ||--o{ bookings : "member_id"
  spaces ||--o{ bookings : "space_id"
  invoices {
    integer id PK
    integer member_id FK
    string invoice_number
    date issued_on
    date due_on
    decimal amount
    string status
  }
  members ||--o{ invoices : "member_id"
```

## Relationships and cardinality

- members (preferred_space_id) → spaces (id): many-to-one; optional parent; parent deletion: SET NULL. A parent can have zero or many matching child records.
- memberships (member_id) → members (id): many-to-one; required parent; parent deletion: RESTRICT. A parent can have zero or many matching child records.
- memberships (plan_id) → plans (id): many-to-one; required parent; parent deletion: RESTRICT. A parent can have zero or many matching child records.
- space_amenities (space_id) → spaces (id): many-to-one; required parent; parent deletion: CASCADE. A parent can have zero or many matching child records.
- space_amenities (amenity_id) → amenities (id): many-to-one; required parent; parent deletion: CASCADE. A parent can have zero or many matching child records.
- bookings (member_id) → members (id): many-to-one; required parent; parent deletion: RESTRICT. A parent can have zero or many matching child records.
- bookings (space_id) → spaces (id): many-to-one; required parent; parent deletion: RESTRICT. A parent can have zero or many matching child records.
- invoices (member_id) → members (id): many-to-one; required parent; parent deletion: RESTRICT. A parent can have zero or many matching child records.

## Business rules

- Unique member emails, plan names, amenity names, invoice numbers, and space names within a location are enforced by UNIQUE keys.
- Positive capacity, nonnegative amounts/hours/rates, permitted lifecycle states, and ordered dates are enforced with CHECK constraints.
- Foreign keys retain member/booking/invoice history through RESTRICT/NO ACTION. Only pure amenity links cascade.
- No overlapping confirmed bookings: the application must lock the space row and query intersecting intervals in the same transaction before insertion. For SQLite use BEGIN IMMEDIATE and serialize writes. Row-level CHECK constraints do not enforce this cross-row rule.
- Back-to-back bookings are valid half-open intervals. Cancelled bookings do not block availability.
- Member data access and location-scoped staff access require application authorization; invoice visibility is limited to billing administrators.
- Member contact details can be anonymized while the member identifier and invoices remain for seven-year billing retention.
- Changing booking and invoice status requires an authorized atomic transaction; payment processing uses idempotency at the integration boundary.

logical-schema.md.content:
# Logical schema

**Design version:** 2 · **Target:** PostgreSQL

Identifiers use portable lowercase snake_case. IDs are application-supplied; no auto-increment allocation is assumed.

## members

Member identity, optional preferred space and contact information, separable from retained financial history.

| Column | Type | Nullable | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | INTEGER | No | — | Application-assigned member identifier |
| full_name | VARCHAR(120) | No | — | Member display name |
| email | VARCHAR(254) | No | — | Unique member contact address |
| joined_on | DATE | No | — | Registration date |
| active | BOOLEAN | No | — | Whether the account may create bookings |
| preferred_space_id | INTEGER | Yes | — | Optional preferred space; preferences never imply a reservation |
| phone | VARCHAR(30) | Yes | — | Optional member phone number in international format |

- **Primary key:** id
- **Unique keys:** (email)
- **Foreign keys:** (preferred_space_id) → spaces(id); ON DELETE SET NULL
- **Checks:** None
- **Declared indexes:** None
- **Automatic indexing:** primary/unique keys are indexed by the engine. The SQL compiler adds an index on each foreign-key column group not already covered by a leading primary/unique/declared index.
- **Sample rows:** 3

## plans

Subscription products with stable pricing and included workspace hours.

| Column | Type | Nullable | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | INTEGER | No | — | Plan identifier |
| name | VARCHAR(80) | No | — | Unique plan label |
| monthly_price | DECIMAL(12,2) | No | — | Monthly price in USD |
| included_hours | INTEGER | No | — | Included monthly booking hours |

- **Primary key:** id
- **Unique keys:** (name)
- **Foreign keys:** None
- **Checks:** plans_nonnegative: monthly_price >= 0 AND included_hours >= 0
- **Declared indexes:** None
- **Automatic indexing:** primary/unique keys are indexed by the engine. The SQL compiler adds an index on each foreign-key column group not already covered by a leading primary/unique/declared index.
- **Sample rows:** 3

## memberships

Effective-dated member subscriptions preserving plan enrollment history.

| Column | Type | Nullable | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | INTEGER | No | — | Membership identifier |
| member_id | INTEGER | No | — | Subscribed member |
| plan_id | INTEGER | No | — | Subscribed plan |
| starts_on | DATE | No | — | First active date |
| ends_on | DATE | Yes | — | Exclusive end date; null means ongoing |

- **Primary key:** id
- **Unique keys:** (member_id, starts_on)
- **Foreign keys:** (member_id) → members(id); ON DELETE RESTRICT; (plan_id) → plans(id); ON DELETE RESTRICT
- **Checks:** memberships_date_order: ends_on IS NULL OR ends_on > starts_on
- **Declared indexes:** None
- **Automatic indexing:** primary/unique keys are indexed by the engine. The SQL compiler adds an index on each foreign-key column group not already covered by a leading primary/unique/declared index.
- **Sample rows:** 3

## spaces

Bookable rooms and desks, each with a location label, capacity and hourly rate.

| Column | Type | Nullable | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | INTEGER | No | — | Space identifier |
| name | VARCHAR(100) | No | — | Name unique inside location |
| location | VARCHAR(100) | No | — | Location label; locations have no other attributes in this scope |
| capacity | INTEGER | No | — | Maximum occupants |
| hourly_rate | DECIMAL(12,2) | No | — | Booking rate in USD per hour |

- **Primary key:** id
- **Unique keys:** (location, name)
- **Foreign keys:** None
- **Checks:** spaces_valid_capacity_rate: capacity > 0 AND hourly_rate >= 0
- **Declared indexes:** None
- **Automatic indexing:** primary/unique keys are indexed by the engine. The SQL compiler adds an index on each foreign-key column group not already covered by a leading primary/unique/declared index.
- **Sample rows:** 3

## amenities

Reusable amenity definitions shared by multiple bookable spaces.

| Column | Type | Nullable | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | INTEGER | No | — | Amenity identifier |
| name | VARCHAR(100) | No | — | Unique amenity label |

- **Primary key:** id
- **Unique keys:** (name)
- **Foreign keys:** None
- **Checks:** None
- **Declared indexes:** None
- **Automatic indexing:** primary/unique keys are indexed by the engine. The SQL compiler adds an index on each foreign-key column group not already covered by a leading primary/unique/declared index.
- **Sample rows:** 3

## space_amenities

Associative relation implementing the many-to-many space-to-amenity relationship.

| Column | Type | Nullable | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| space_id | INTEGER | No | — | Equipped space |
| amenity_id | INTEGER | No | — | Available amenity |

- **Primary key:** space_id, amenity_id
- **Unique keys:** None beyond primary key
- **Foreign keys:** (space_id) → spaces(id); ON DELETE CASCADE; (amenity_id) → amenities(id); ON DELETE CASCADE
- **Checks:** None
- **Declared indexes:** None
- **Automatic indexing:** primary/unique keys are indexed by the engine. The SQL compiler adds an index on each foreign-key column group not already covered by a leading primary/unique/declared index.
- **Sample rows:** 5

## bookings

UTC reservation intervals with lifecycle state and an optional member-supplied note.

| Column | Type | Nullable | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | INTEGER | No | — | Booking identifier |
| member_id | INTEGER | No | — | Booking owner |
| space_id | INTEGER | No | — | Reserved space |
| starts_at | TIMESTAMP | No | — | Inclusive start, UTC |
| ends_at | TIMESTAMP | No | — | Exclusive end, UTC |
| status | VARCHAR(20) | No | — | Reservation lifecycle |
| note | TEXT | Yes | — | Optional booking request |

- **Primary key:** id
- **Unique keys:** None beyond primary key
- **Foreign keys:** (member_id) → members(id); ON DELETE RESTRICT; (space_id) → spaces(id); ON DELETE RESTRICT
- **Checks:** bookings_interval: ends_at > starts_at; bookings_status: status IN ('confirmed', 'completed', 'cancelled')
- **Declared indexes:** bookings_availability_idx (space_id, starts_at, ends_at); bookings_member_history_idx (member_id, starts_at)
- **Automatic indexing:** primary/unique keys are indexed by the engine. The SQL compiler adds an index on each foreign-key column group not already covered by a leading primary/unique/declared index.
- **Sample rows:** 3

## invoices

Retained member invoices independent of optional booking activity; no payment card data.

| Column | Type | Nullable | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | INTEGER | No | — | Invoice identifier |
| member_id | INTEGER | No | — | Billed member retained as an anonymizable FK target |
| invoice_number | VARCHAR(40) | No | — | Unique business invoice reference |
| issued_on | DATE | No | — | Issue date |
| due_on | DATE | No | — | Payment deadline |
| amount | DECIMAL(12,2) | No | — | Invoice amount in USD |
| status | VARCHAR(20) | No | — | Payment lifecycle |

- **Primary key:** id
- **Unique keys:** (invoice_number)
- **Foreign keys:** (member_id) → members(id); ON DELETE RESTRICT
- **Checks:** invoices_amount: amount >= 0; invoices_dates: due_on >= issued_on; invoices_status: status IN ('draft', 'paid', 'overdue')
- **Declared indexes:** invoices_status_due_idx (status, due_on)
- **Automatic indexing:** primary/unique keys are indexed by the engine. The SQL compiler adds an index on each foreign-key column group not already covered by a leading primary/unique/declared index.
- **Sample rows:** 3

## Relational schema diagram

```mermaid
erDiagram
  members {
    INTEGER id PK
    VARCHAR_120_ full_name
    VARCHAR_254_ email
    DATE joined_on
    BOOLEAN active
    INTEGER preferred_space_id FK
    VARCHAR_30_ phone
  }
  spaces |o--o{ members : "preferred_space_id"
  plans {
    INTEGER id PK
    VARCHAR_80_ name
    DECIMAL_12_2_ monthly_price
    INTEGER included_hours
  }
  memberships {
    INTEGER id PK
    INTEGER member_id FK
    INTEGER plan_id FK
    DATE starts_on
    DATE ends_on
  }
  members ||--o{ memberships : "member_id"
  plans ||--o{ memberships : "plan_id"
  spaces {
    INTEGER id PK
    VARCHAR_100_ name
    VARCHAR_100_ location
    INTEGER capacity
    DECIMAL_12_2_ hourly_rate
  }
  amenities {
    INTEGER id PK
    VARCHAR_100_ name
  }
  space_amenities {
    INTEGER space_id PK,FK
    INTEGER amenity_id PK,FK
  }
  spaces ||--o{ space_amenities : "space_id"
  amenities ||--o{ space_amenities : "amenity_id"
  bookings {
    INTEGER id PK
    INTEGER member_id FK
    INTEGER space_id FK
    TIMESTAMP starts_at
    TIMESTAMP ends_at
    VARCHAR_20_ status
    TEXT note
  }
  members ||--o{ bookings : "member_id"
  spaces ||--o{ bookings : "space_id"
  invoices {
    INTEGER id PK
    INTEGER member_id FK
    VARCHAR_40_ invoice_number
    DATE issued_on
    DATE due_on
    DECIMAL_12_2_ amount
    VARCHAR_20_ status
  }
  members ||--o{ invoices : "member_id"
```

## Security and privacy

- No passwords, payment cards, or real personal data are seeded. Example contact addresses use example.org.
- Separate member, location-staff, and billing-administrator permissions in the application and production database roles.
- Encrypt transport and backups; minimize contact data and audit access to billing information.
- Retain invoices seven years and booking history two years; anonymize member contact information without breaking retained FKs.
- Member phone numbers are optional private contact details; restrict access and include them in anonymization.

normalization.md.content:
# Normalization analysis

**Design version:** 2 · **Target:** PostgreSQL

## Method

1NF requires atomic attributes and unique rows. 2NF excludes partial dependencies on part of a composite candidate key. 3NF excludes non-key transitive dependencies. Surrogate primary keys alone do not prove 3NF. The following dependency claims must be reviewed against the actual business semantics.

## members

### Functional dependencies

- id → full_name, email, joined_on, active, preferred_space_id, phone
- email → id, full_name, joined_on, active, preferred_space_id, phone

### Normal-form assessment

1NF: each column contains an atomic value. 2NF: the single-column primary key has no partial dependencies. 3NF: non-key attributes depend on a candidate key, not on another non-key attribute; related mutable facts live in their own relations.

## plans

### Functional dependencies

- id → name, monthly_price, included_hours
- name → id, monthly_price, included_hours

### Normal-form assessment

1NF: each column contains an atomic value. 2NF: the single-column primary key has no partial dependencies. 3NF: non-key attributes depend on a candidate key, not on another non-key attribute; related mutable facts live in their own relations.

## memberships

### Functional dependencies

- id → member_id, plan_id, starts_on, ends_on
- (member_id, starts_on) → id, plan_id, ends_on

### Normal-form assessment

1NF: each column contains an atomic value. 2NF: the single-column primary key has no partial dependencies. 3NF: non-key attributes depend on a candidate key, not on another non-key attribute; related mutable facts live in their own relations.

## spaces

### Functional dependencies

- id → name, location, capacity, hourly_rate
- (location, name) → id, capacity, hourly_rate

### Normal-form assessment

1NF: each column contains an atomic value. 2NF: the single-column primary key has no partial dependencies. 3NF: non-key attributes depend on a candidate key, not on another non-key attribute; related mutable facts live in their own relations.

## amenities

### Functional dependencies

- id → name
- name → id

### Normal-form assessment

1NF: each column contains an atomic value. 2NF: the single-column primary key has no partial dependencies. 3NF: non-key attributes depend on a candidate key, not on another non-key attribute; related mutable facts live in their own relations.

## space_amenities

### Functional dependencies

- (space_id, amenity_id) is the sole candidate key; there are no non-key attributes

### Normal-form assessment

1NF: each link is atomic and unique. 2NF: there are no non-key attributes to depend on part of the composite key. 3NF and BCNF: no nontrivial functional dependency has a non-superkey determinant.

## bookings

### Functional dependencies

- id → every non-key attribute

### Normal-form assessment

1NF: each column contains an atomic value. 2NF: the single-column primary key has no partial dependencies. 3NF: non-key attributes depend on a candidate key, not on another non-key attribute; related mutable facts live in their own relations.

## invoices

### Functional dependencies

- id → member_id, invoice_number, issued_on, due_on, amount, status
- invoice_number → id, member_id, issued_on, due_on, amount, status

### Normal-form assessment

1NF: each column contains an atomic value. 2NF: the single-column primary key has no partial dependencies. 3NF: non-key attributes depend on a candidate key, not on another non-key attribute; related mutable facts live in their own relations.

## Deliberate denormalization

No deliberate denormalization. Every table is intended to satisfy at least 3NF.

## Validation boundary

Execution checks prove syntax and constraint/seed compatibility, not the truth of functional dependencies. A human must confirm semantic normalization.

assumptions.md.name: assumptions.md
assumptions.md.content:
# Assumptions and remaining ambiguity

**Design version:** 2 · **Target:** PostgreSQL

- The demonstration is deliberately scoped: locations are labels with no address/manager facts; introduce a locations entity if those attributes become requirements.
- All timestamps represent UTC; timezone conversion occurs at the client boundary.
- A member can have historical memberships. Transactional policy prevents overlapping active membership intervals.
- Amounts use USD and invoices are standalone billed totals, not aggregates of unstored invoice-line records.
- Included hours are a plan allowance; consumption accounting and payment processing are outside this specified sample scope.
- Plans should be versioned rather than mutating prices that need historical interpretation.
- Identifiers are assigned explicitly by the application, not by a sequence.

## Operational assumptions

- Run schema.sql in an existing empty database with appropriate CREATE privileges. Do not run it against production.
- Seed data is synthetic and contains no real personal information.
- Sample data is not an exhaustive performance or security test.
- Monetary decimal values are illustrative; production applications should use exact decimal serialization.
- All generated files derive from one canonical design model, included as design.json in the export.
- This is the explicitly labelled offline coworking example, not an LLM interpretation of an arbitrary brief.

schema.sql.name: schema.sql
schema.sql.content:
-- Lumina coworking platform
-- Target: PostgreSQL. Run in a new, empty database.
-- IDs are explicitly supplied by the application; no identity/sequence allocation is assumed.

CREATE TABLE "plans" (
  "id" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "name" VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
  "monthly_price" DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
  "included_hours" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY ("id"),
  UNIQUE ("name"),
  CONSTRAINT "plans_nonnegative" CHECK (monthly_price >= 0 AND included_hours >= 0)
);

CREATE TABLE "spaces" (
  "id" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "name" VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  "location" VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  "capacity" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "hourly_rate" DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY ("id"),
  UNIQUE ("location", "name"),
  CONSTRAINT "spaces_valid_capacity_rate" CHECK (capacity > 0 AND hourly_rate >= 0)
);

CREATE TABLE "members" (
  "id" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "full_name" VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
  "email" VARCHAR(254) NOT NULL,
  "joined_on" DATE NOT NULL,
  "active" BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  "preferred_space_id" INTEGER,
  "phone" VARCHAR(30),
  PRIMARY KEY ("id"),
  UNIQUE ("email"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("preferred_space_id") REFERENCES "spaces" ("id") ON DELETE SET NULL
);

CREATE INDEX "fk_members_0_fi7imo" ON "members" ("preferred_space_id");

CREATE TABLE "memberships" (
  "id" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "member_id" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "plan_id" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "starts_on" DATE NOT NULL,
  "ends_on" DATE,
  PRIMARY KEY ("id"),
  UNIQUE ("member_id", "starts_on"),
  CONSTRAINT "memberships_date_order" CHECK (ends_on IS NULL OR ends_on > starts_on),
  FOREIGN KEY ("member_id") REFERENCES "members" ("id") ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  FOREIGN KEY ("plan_id") REFERENCES "plans" ("id") ON DELETE RESTRICT
);

CREATE INDEX "fk_memberships_1_1gk8tjy" ON "memberships" ("plan_id");

CREATE TABLE "amenities" (
  "id" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "name" VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY ("id"),
  UNIQUE ("name")
);

CREATE TABLE "space_amenities" (
  "space_id" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "amenity_id" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY ("space_id", "amenity_id"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("space_id") REFERENCES "spaces" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
  FOREIGN KEY ("amenity_id") REFERENCES "amenities" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE INDEX "fk_space_amenities_1_nxxwuh" ON "space_amenities" ("amenity_id");

CREATE TABLE "bookings" (
  "id" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "member_id" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "space_id" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "starts_at" TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
  "ends_at" TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
  "status" VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  "note" TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY ("id"),
  CONSTRAINT "bookings_interval" CHECK (ends_at > starts_at),
  CONSTRAINT "bookings_status" CHECK (status IN ('confirmed', 'completed', 'cancelled')),
  FOREIGN KEY ("member_id") REFERENCES "members" ("id") ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  FOREIGN KEY ("space_id") REFERENCES "spaces" ("id") ON DELETE RESTRICT
);

CREATE INDEX "bookings_availability_idx" ON "bookings" ("space_id", "starts_at", "ends_at");

CREATE INDEX "bookings_member_history_idx" ON "bookings" ("member_id", "starts_at");

CREATE TABLE "invoices" (
  "id" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "member_id" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "invoice_number" VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
  "issued_on" DATE NOT NULL,
  "due_on" DATE NOT NULL,
  "amount" DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
  "status" VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY ("id"),
  UNIQUE ("invoice_number"),
  CONSTRAINT "invoices_amount" CHECK (amount >= 0),
  CONSTRAINT "invoices_dates" CHECK (due_on >= issued_on),
  CONSTRAINT "invoices_status" CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'paid', 'overdue')),
  FOREIGN KEY ("member_id") REFERENCES "members" ("id") ON DELETE RESTRICT
);

CREATE INDEX "invoices_status_due_idx" ON "invoices" ("status", "due_on");

CREATE INDEX "fk_invoices_0_1vs3wex" ON "invoices" ("member_id");

  "summary": "Members need full name, unique email, joined date, active flag, and an optional preferred space. Plans have unique names, monthly price, and included hours. Spaces have a location, unique name per location, capacity and hourly rate. Bookings use UTC start/end and confirmed/completed/cancelled states. Invoices track issue/due dates, amount and draft/paid/overdue states.

Members have many historical memberships; a membership has one member and one plan. A member can optionally choose one preferred space; a space can be preferred by many members. Members make many bookings, each for one space. Spaces share amenities through a many-to-many link. Each invoice belongs to one member; invoices can exist without bookings.

5,000 initial members, 100,000 bookings/year, 3 locations growing to 10, around 30% annual data growth. Keep invoices for seven years and bookings for two years.

Frequent availability searches by location and time, daily staff booking lists, member booking history, monthly occupancy, and overdue-invoice reports. Roughly 20 reads per write.

No overlapping confirmed bookings for a space. The application serializes reservations with a per-space lock and an overlap query inside the same transaction. Invoice status transitions are atomic and idempotent. Around 50 concurrent reservations at peak.

Members only access their own records. Staff can manage bookings for assigned locations; only billing admins see invoices. No payment card details or passwords stored here. Anonymize contact data instead of deleting retained billing evidence.

Booking end must follow start; dates use UTC. Capacity must be positive, rates and invoice amounts nonnegative, emails unique, and due date cannot precede issue date. Cancelled bookings remain for audit and do not block availability.

Yes, lock the space row during each booking transaction and reject any intersecting confirmed interval. Back-to-back reservations are allowed. Members can have multiple non-overlapping memberships over time; enforcing membership interval exclusivity is also a transaction-level policy.

Retain invoice records for seven years, keep a minimal anonymized member record as their FK target, and store all booking timestamps as UTC. Cancellation retains the original reservation and its status."
